newsitem.title: USA: Utah Medical sees lower Q4 sales, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Utah Medical sees lower Q4 sales, earnings.

text.p: Utah Medical Products Inc said Friday it will have lower-than-expected fourth quarter sales and earnings because of softer-than-expected year-end demand from customers.
The company also said the 1997 first quarter will see "an even greater unfavorable comparison" with the year-earlier quarter.
Despite these projections, the company said it believes it will have positive full-year results for both 1996 and 1997.
It said 1996 net after-tax earnings and earnings per share should set a new calendar year record, and that it is planning on another record in 1997 per share earnings.
Utah Medical shares were up 1/4 at 13-7/8 early Friday afternoon.
Company officials were not available for comment.
The company said sales of its new obstetrics tool, Cordguard, remained "disappointing and immaterial" to fourth quarter results.
Additionally, it said sales of its new gynecological products have not begun to offset a rapid sales decline in its critical care products.
It also said sales to a new distribution partner in the U.S., Vital Signs Inc, were "well below" expectations.
Richens said earnings for the 1996 first quarter were $0.25 per share. "We will not be able to duplicate that" in the 1997 first quarter, he said.
The company attributed its 1997 first quarter projection to lower sales to Baxter International Inc and costs for changing its U.S. distribution system.
It said first quarter sales to Baxter are expected to be about $300,000, down from $3.8 million a year earlier.
It also said it would not see a large payment for its technology in the first quarter. Such a payment added about $0.05 a share to 1996 first quarter earnings, it said.
